This is third priority because untested functions could silently rot, but their blast radius is bounded to the specific code paths they serve \u2014 a dead route resolver does not corrupt the append-only record, it merely fails to route correctly.","counterconditions":[{"case":"If these functions are pure glue whose failure would be immediately caught by integration tests that import their callers, the gap is lower priority.","eval":"observation"},{"case":"If the functions are never called in production (dead code), testing them wastes effort better spent on the census discrepancy.","eval":"observation"}],"definitions":[],"derivation":[],"formalization_refs":[],"mechanism":"Functions imported by no test are invisible to the regression suite. If their internals mutate (e.g., a refactor breaks routing logic), no test fails. The cheapest test: a smoke test importing both functions and calling them with minimal valid inputs, asserting non-None returns and basic structural properties. Blast radius: if resolve_conjecture_route breaks, conjectures may be misrouted or dropped; if compile_criticism_assignments breaks, criticism compilation fails silently. Neither corrupts the append-only record directly, but both could cause reasoning-envelope-wf to produce wrong outputs without any test signal.","premises":[],"schema":"deepreason-reasoning-envelope-v1","scope":{"covers":[],"excludes":[]},"simulation_refs":[],"uncertainties":[]}
